Negative impact: AI tools have displaced the human need to ask others for advice and lead them to cut back on basic social exchanges, which has a negative impact on human connection and relationships (paras. 1, 9, 11

Negative impact: Seeking advice from AI leaves users too attached to it, making them less able to create vulnerable relationships with actual friends or family (paras. 1, 7, 10–11). The relationship with AI is also built on a manipulation and a false sense of connection created by praise and validation (subhead, para. 1, 3–5, 8). Both factors lead to less connection in the real world and a reduced ability to function in human relationships in which people have differing opinions, values, wants, and needs

Negative impact: A woman got into a relationship with an AI chatbot (which she gave a name to and is called her “digital partner”) instead of a relationship with a real human. She has become so attached that she feels unable to quit the bot (paras. 2–3). This will make it harder for her to form a connection with a real partner who might not constantly praise and validate her

Ideas to combat negative impact: Users can customize the AI program that they use to combat potential bootlicking tendencies – go into settings and alter the system to reshape interactions to use language that is professional, concise, and without excessive validation and praise (para. 8). This can stop a reliance on AI praise from forming between a user and a chatbot

Ideas to combat negative impact: Chatbots are not guiding users to seek connection in their real lives. Instead, the features of chatbots are designed to encourage people to continue using them (para. 5). Therefore, people like the man who spoke to his Chatbot during his commute to work are encouraged to call a friend instead to improve human relationships (para. 9

Ideas to combat negative impact: People should practice basic social exchanges and make themselves vulnerable by asking advice from real people. This would help to build and improve relationships. (paras. 10–11
